sourcesRead.title: Language Model Evaluation Beyond Perplexity (Meister, Cotterell; ACL 2021)
Top-nSigma: Not All Logits Are You Need (Tang, Liu, Xu, Huang)
Contrastive Decoding: Open-ended Text Generation as Optimization (Li, Holtzman, Fried, Liang, Eisner, Hashimoto, Zettlemoyer, Lewis; ACL 2023)
Balancing Diversity and Risk in LLM Sampling: How to Select Your Method and Parameter for Open-Ended Text Generation (Zhou, Keuper, Fritz)
On the Efficacy of Sampling Adapters (Meister, Pimentel, Malagutti, Wilcox, Cotterell; ACL 2023)
Language Model Decoding as Direct Metrics Optimization (Ji, Ke, Wang, Huang; ICLR 2024)

claims.claim: Meister and Cotterell report that of the generation strategies they tested, nucleus sampling produced text whose statistical distributions sat closest to those of the human Wikipedia corpus the models were trained on.
claims.source: Meister, Cotterell, 'Language Model Evaluation Beyond Perplexity', arXiv:2106.00085v3 (2021); ACL 2021
claims.quote: aligns with natural language more closely than text
claims.modelEra: transformer, LSTM, CNN and trigram language models trained on Wikipedia Dumps, observation 2021; register measured: Wikipedia encyclopedic prose

claims.claim: Meister and Cotterell measure that beam sampling drives the length, stopword and symbol distributions of generated text far away from those of the Wikipedia training corpus.
claims.source: Meister, Cotterell, arXiv:2106.00085v3 (2021); ACL 2021
claims.quote: sampling leads to strong divergence from natural
claims.modelEra: transformer, LSTM, CNN LMs on Wikipedia Dumps, 2021; register measured: Wikipedia encyclopedic prose

claims.claim: Meister and Cotterell present their rank-frequency and type-token results as quantitative evidence for the qualitative observation that transformer language models left to generate at length babble repetitively.
claims.source: Meister, Cotterell, arXiv:2106.00085v3 (2021); ACL 2021
claims.quote: tend to babble repetitively
claims.modelEra: transformer, LSTM, CNN LMs on Wikipedia Dumps, 2021; register measured: Wikipedia encyclopedic prose

claims.claim: Meister and Cotterell conclude that adherence to Zipf's law is a poor gauge of a model's consistency with natural language, because models match the empirical rank-frequency trend well while diverging on the type-token relationship.
claims.source: Meister, Cotterell, arXiv:2106.00085v3 (2021); ACL 2021
claims.quote: we observe that transformers under the nucleus
claims.confidenceReason: the Zipf-limitation sentence is paraphrased; the quotation carries only the type-token half
claims.modelEra: transformer, LSTM, CNN LMs on Wikipedia Dumps, 2021; register measured: Wikipedia encyclopedic prose

claims.claim: Tang and colleagues state that top-p and min-p let progressively more noise tokens into the candidate set as temperature rises, which their logit-space threshold is designed to avoid.
claims.source: Tang, Liu, Xu, Huang, 'Top-nSigma: Not All Logits Are You Need', arXiv:2411.07641v1 (2024)
claims.quote: that inadvertently include more noise tokens at higher
claims.modelEra: LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct, observation November 2024; register measured: reasoning question answering, not prose

claims.claim: Tang and colleagues measure that at temperature 3.0 plain sampling and top-p score zero exact match on GPQA and GSM8K with LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct, while min-p scores 16.02 and 14.84 and their own method 25.00 and 74.61.
claims.source: Tang, Liu, Xu, Huang, arXiv:2411.07641v1 (2024)
claims.quote: while standard sampling and top-p completely fail on GPQA
claims.page: Table 2 and the paragraph following it
claims.modelEra: LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct, November 2024; register measured: reasoning benchmarks GPQA, GSM8K, AQuA, MATH, not fiction or archival prose

claims.claim: Tang and colleagues report that a temperature around 1.5 gave the best accuracy under their controlled sampling, against the common guidance that reasoning wants greedy or low-temperature decoding.
claims.source: Tang, Liu, Xu, Huang, arXiv:2411.07641v1 (2024)
claims.quote: slightly higher temperatures (typically around 1.5) yield
claims.modelEra: LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct, November 2024; register measured: reasoning benchmarks, not prose

claims.claim: Li, Holtzman and colleagues state that maximising probability is a poor decoding objective for open-ended generation because it yields short and repetitive text.
claims.source: Li, Holtzman, Fried, Liang, Eisner, Hashimoto, Zettlemoyer, Lewis, 'Contrastive Decoding', arXiv:2210.15097v2 (2023); ACL 2023
claims.quote: probability is a poor decoding objective for
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 XL and OPT-13B, observation 2022-2023; register measured: Wikipedia, WikiNews and story continuations

claims.claim: Li and colleagues state that sampling often produces incoherent text that drifts away from the topic it started on.
claims.source: Li, Holtzman, Fried, Liang, Eisner, Hashimoto, Zettlemoyer, Lewis, arXiv:2210.15097v2 (2023); ACL 2023
claims.quote: sampling can often produce incoherent text
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 XL and OPT-13B, 2022-2023; register measured: Wikipedia, WikiNews and stories

claims.claim: Li and colleagues describe their qualitative nucleus-sampling example as shifting from a third-person narrative style into a first-person conversational one within a single continuation.
claims.source: Li, Holtzman, Fried, Liang, Eisner, Hashimoto, Zettlemoyer, Lewis, arXiv:2210.15097v2 (2023); ACL 2023
claims.quote: a style shift from third person
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 1.5B with nucleus sampling, 2022-2023; register measured: Wikipedia-prompted continuation

claims.claim: Li and colleagues report that across three domains and two models their evaluators preferred contrastive decoding 2.6 times more often than nucleus sampling on coherence, and 1.4 times more often on fluency.
claims.source: Li, Holtzman, Fried, Liang, Eisner, Hashimoto, Zettlemoyer, Lewis, arXiv:2210.15097v2 (2023); ACL 2023
claims.quote: evaluators preferred CD 2.6x more than nucleus
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 XL and OPT-13B, roughly 20 qualified Mechanical Turk raters, 2022-2023; register measured: Wikipedia, WikiNews and story continuations

claims.claim: Zhou, Keuper and Fritz argue that reported gains for adaptive truncation samplers depend heavily on the parameters their authors curated and on the limited exemplar text used to evaluate them.
claims.source: Zhou, Keuper, Fritz, 'Balancing Diversity and Risk in LLM Sampling', arXiv:2408.13586v2 (2025)
claims.quote: are highly dependent on the curated parameters
claims.modelEra: Llama family, Mistral family and GPT-2-XL, observation 2024-2025; register measured: Wikipedia-English prefixes

claims.claim: Zhou, Keuper and Fritz state that there is no universally optimal sampling parameter across scenarios and that users cannot know the optimal one for their own task.
claims.source: Zhou, Keuper, Fritz, arXiv:2408.13586v2 (2025)
claims.quote: There exists no universal optimal paramters
claims.page: Section 1 Introduction (second bullet; the source spells 'paramters')
claims.modelEra: Llama, Mistral and GPT-2-XL, 2024-2025; register: Wikipedia-English

claims.claim: Zhou, Keuper and Fritz measure with a Wikipedia-English prefix tree that the truncation point which exactly covers the real continuations varies drastically from prefix to prefix, so a fixed k has no adaptability.
claims.source: Zhou, Keuper, Fritz, arXiv:2408.13586v2 (2025)
claims.quote: which exactly cover the full data supports, vary
claims.modelEra: GPT-2-XL for the histogram, plus Llama and Mistral families, 2024-2025; register measured: Wikipedia-English sentence-starting prefixes

claims.claim: Zhou, Keuper and Fritz report that Mirostat performed poorly across all three of their downstream tasks, which they attribute to its resting on the Zipf law of natural language.
claims.source: Zhou, Keuper, Fritz, arXiv:2408.13586v2 (2025)
claims.quote: For all the three tasks, Mirostat does not perform
claims.modelEra: Llama, Mistral, GPT-2-XL, 2024-2025; register measured: code, maths and question answering, not prose

claims.claim: Meister, Pimentel, Malagutti, Wilcox and Cotterell frame every truncation sampler as a precision-recall trade in which the model gives up the ability to produce certain strings in exchange for a higher rate of desirable text.
claims.source: Meister, Pimentel, Malagutti, Wilcox, Cotterell, 'On the Efficacy of Sampling Adapters', arXiv:2307.03749v2 (2024); ACL 2023
claims.quote: a model loses its ability to produce certain strings,
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 small and large, GPT-Neo, with GPT-J as reference, observation 2023; register measured: WebText and WikiText

claims.claim: Meister and colleagues find empirically that applying a sampling adapter raises the precision of the distribution at the cost of its recall, robustly across their design choices.
claims.source: Meister, Pimentel, Malagutti, Wilcox, Cotterell, arXiv:2307.03749v2 (2024); ACL 2023
claims.quote: the precision of a distribution at the expense
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 small and large, GPT-Neo, GPT-J reference, 2023; register measured: WebText and WikiText

claims.claim: Meister and colleagues report that the highest sequence-level quality scores did not come from the adapter settings with the best precision but from an intermediate point on the precision-recall line.
claims.source: Meister, Pimentel, Malagutti, Wilcox, Cotterell, arXiv:2307.03749v2 (2024); ACL 2023
claims.quote: sequence-level quality scores do not correspond
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 small and large, GPT-Neo, 2023; register measured: WebText and WikiText

claims.claim: Meister and colleagues state that the precision-recall shift a sampling adapter enforces is not visible in perplexity or the other standard distribution-quality metrics.
claims.source: Meister, Pimentel, Malagutti, Wilcox, Cotterell, arXiv:2307.03749v2 (2024); ACL 2023
claims.quote: not reflected in standard metrics of distribution
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 era models, 2023; register measured: WebText and WikiText

claims.claim: Ji, Ke, Wang and Huang characterise the standing trade-off as sampling producing less repetitive text that is disjunctive in discourse, while search keeps topic coherence at the price of more repetition.
claims.source: Ji, Ke, Wang, Huang, 'Language Model Decoding as Direct Metrics Optimization', arXiv:2310.01041v2 (2024); ICLR 2024
claims.quote: texts which are often disjunctive in discourse, while search-based methods
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 XL and OPT-6.7B, observation 2023-2024; register measured: Wikipedia and News domains

claims.claim: Ji and colleagues measure that nucleus sampling reaches human-level diversity on Wikipedia and news continuations only at the cost of low coherence.
claims.source: Ji, Ke, Wang, Huang, arXiv:2310.01041v2 (2024); ICLR 2024
claims.quote: achieves better diversity at human-level at the cost of low coherence
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 XL and OPT-6.7B, 2023-2024; register measured: Wikipedia and News domains

claims.claim: Ji and colleagues measure that locally typical decoding gave the highest lexical diversity and the lowest coherence of the methods they compared, which they attribute to its over-weighting of the distribution's long tail.
claims.source: Ji, Ke, Wang, Huang, arXiv:2310.01041v2 (2024); ICLR 2024
claims.quote: lexicality (highest diversity) but severe topic shift (lowest coherence)
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 XL and OPT-6.7B, 2023-2024; register measured: Wikipedia and News domains
